claims: note/fang-2026-n2-n-1.md, draft v0.9 of 2026-10-18, the text of DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23463481 by the author's comment of 19 October on jlevy/squares#603: Theorem 1, s(n^2 - n + 1) < n for every integer n >= 15.

Theorem 2: let n >= 15 and p, q >= 0 integers with 16p + 21q <= n - 15; then n^2 - n + 1 + p + 2q unit squares pack in a square of side less than n; in particular s(n^2 - n + F(n)) < n with F(n) = 1 + max{p + 2q : p, q in Z>=0, 16p + 21q <= n - 15}.

The proof (Section 2): Lemma 3, the four-piece gluing of Arslanov, Mustafin and Shangitbayev, at a common squeeze d; Proposition 4, the rectangles R (257 squares in 17 x 16) and R' (443 in 22 x 21); Proposition 5, the base packings of n^2 - n + 1 squares for 15 <= n <= 26 and of m^2 - m squares for 11 <= m <= 14, every piece 1/10000-squeezable; and an induction on n by steps of 16 and 21, every composite of side n - 1/10000, scaled to a strict certificate of side n - 1/20000.

Section 6, Formal verification: Lean 4 (TheSnakeFang/squarepack-lean at 947bdae, proof sources of 837eca1) formalises Theorem 1 and the maximum of the two unmixed bounds of Theorem 2, jExc n = max ((n + 1) / 16) (1 + 2 * ((n - 15) / 21)); the mixed-step form of Theorem 2 is not formalised; #print axioms lists propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.
README.md at the pin: 'Lean 4 formalisation of Theorem 1 and the unmixed bounds of Theorem 2'.
